blocks.content: STATE LEGISLATURE

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The State Legislature provisions are specified under Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution.
Currently, only 6 states have a bicameral legislature: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the directly elected lower house with a maximum strength of 500 and a minimum of 60.
The Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is a permanent upper house that cannot be dissolved, with 1/3rd of its members retiring every 2 years.
Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority.
Money Bills can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly, and the Speaker decides whether a bill is a Money Bill.

blocks.content: The State Legislature is one of the most important organs of the State Government in India. It represents the democratic will of the people at the state level and performs law-making, financial, and supervisory functions.

Just as Parliament functions at the national level, the State Legislature functions at the state level. It plays a vital role in ensuring democracy, accountability, and good governance within the State.
The provisions relating to State Legislature are mentioned in Part VI of the Indian Constitution (Articles 168–212).

The Legislative Assembly is the lower house and the most powerful body in the State Legislature. Composition:

items:

  • Minimum strength – 60 (can be less in smaller states)
  • Term – 5 years
  • Can be dissolved earlier by Governor

blocks.content: LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL (VIDHAN PARISHAD) – DETAILED
The Legislative Council is the upper house of the State Legislature. Nature:

items:
• Permanent House
  • Cannot be dissolved
  • 1/3 members retire every 2 years

blocks.content: Composition:
Mode of Election:

items:
• 1/3 elected by MLAs
  • 1/3 by local authorities
  • 1/12 by teachers
  • 1/12 by graduates
  • 1/6 nominated by Governor

blocks.content: The Council acts as a revising and advisory body.

ROLE OF GOVERNOR IN STATE LEGISLATURE
The Governor is an integral part of the State Legislature. Powers:

items:
• Summons and prorogues legislature
  • Addresses the first session
  • Gives assent to bills
  • Can reserve bills for President
  • Can dissolve Legislative Assembly

blocks.content: CREATION AND ABOLITION OF LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL

items: Article 169: Empowers Parliament to create or abolish a Legislative Council based on a special majority resolution passed by the State Assembly.
Money Bill Restrictions: Money Bills originate exclusively in the Legislative Assembly, and the Legislative Council can delay them for a maximum of only 14 days.
Composition of Legislative Council: 1/3 elected by MLAs, 1/3 by local authorities, 1/12 by teachers, 1/12 by graduates, and 1/6 nominated by the Governor.
Executive Control: Only the Legislative Assembly can pass a No-Confidence Motion to remove the Council of Ministers; the Legislative Council lacks this power.

blocks.content: CONCLUSION
The State Legislature is the backbone of democracy at the state level.
It ensures accountability, transparency and participation of people in governance.
A strong and effective State Legislature is essential for the success of Indian federalism and democracy.
